headline: PAGASA Raises Red Rainfall Warning for Zambales and Parts of Bataan
seoTitle: Red Rainfall Warning for Zambales, Parts of Bataan | FMB News
seoDescription: PAGASA placed Zambales and parts of Bataan under a Red rainfall warning at 11 a.m. on August 28 as Habagat continued to threaten flooding in Luzon.
deck: Serious flooding was expected in Red-warning areas while several Central Luzon provinces remained under Orange alerts and Metro Manila stayed under Yellow.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: PAGASA placed Zambales and the Bataan municipalities of Morong, Hermosa and Dinalupihan under a Red rainfall warning at 11 a.m. Friday, August 28, because of the Southwest Monsoon or Habagat.

The weather bureau said serious flooding was expected in flood-prone areas covered by the Red warning. Pampanga, Tarlac, Bulacan, other parts of Bataan and specified areas of Nueva Ecija were under Orange, where flooding remained threatening.

sections.heading: Other warning areas
paragraphs: Metro Manila, Rizal, parts of Cavite and Batangas, and the remaining specified areas of Nueva Ecija were under a Yellow warning at 11 a.m. PAGASA said flooding was possible in flood-prone communities in those areas.

Northern Luzon was covered by a separate 11 a.m. rainfall advisory reporting persistent rain over La Union, Benguet, Ilocos Sur and several nearby areas. That advisory did not assign the Orange or Red warning levels used by the NCR regional office.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: PAGASA's broader heavy-rainfall outlook, issued at 11 a.m., forecast 100 to 200 millimeters over La Union, Benguet, Bataan, Zambales and Occidental Mindoro through the remainder of August 28. A rainfall outlook covers a longer period and should not be confused with the shorter-fuse regional warning colors.

A low-pressure area east of Northern Luzon was also being monitored. Its development and track remained uncertain, while hazardous monsoon rain could continue regardless of whether the disturbance became a named storm.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Repeated rain can quickly worsen flooding and slope instability. Communities near rivers, drainage channels and steep terrain should follow evacuation, road-closure and safety instructions from local disaster authorities.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Rainfall-warning levels and covered municipalities can change within hours. Residents should rely on the latest PAGASA regional warning, river-basin advisory and local disaster-office instruction rather than an earlier color level.
